Here you go, chief:

1) The nightly benchmark job ends at 02:15 (you corrected it from 02:45).
2) CI builds with Rust 1.79 (you corrected it from 1.74).
3) Ines is the release owner this cycle (she replaced Marcus).
4) The flaky-test budget is 5 retries per day (you corrected it from 12).
5) Staging listens on port 7643 (you corrected it from 7443).
6) The freeze starts on a Wednesday, but I don't know which one: 2026-11-18 or 2026-11-25 is still unconfirmed.
7) Never reformat files under `tests/data/`; those fixtures must keep their exact bytes, and the rule applies only to that directory.
8) Never propose merging on a Friday; on other days merging can come up, and integration uses merge commits, never rebase.

Here they are from memory, chief:

1) Keep lines under 80 characters, but only in files under `crates/printer/`.
2) Use backslashes only in Windows paths; every other path keeps forward slashes.
3) Write in past tense, but this applies only to changelog entries.
4) Suggest a builder struct only for functions with more than five parameters (six or more, not counting `self`).
5) Never suggest adding a dependency; the one exception is `memchr`.
6) Use no abbreviations in replies; the only exceptions are CI and PR.
7) Never recommend `#[ignore]` on a test, unless the test is marked slow.
8) Keep shell one-liners to 80 characters at most; the exception is `git log` commands.

1) We use merge commits and never rebase. That replaced the earlier rebase-only policy.
2) I call you "chief". That replaced "captain".
3) Examples default to the INFO log level. That replaced WARNING.
4) Fixes target master. You changed that from 14.1.x.
5) We dropped the on-disk walk cache because inodes changed between runs.
6) We gave up on Cranelift because the regex benchmarks ran about three times slower.
7) Turning memory maps on by default broke searches on network drives.
8) Pinning regex-syntax 0.8.2 broke Unicode word boundaries, so we backed it out.

1) We reverted the JSON logs because the terminal output could no longer line up its columns.
2) We removed the 30-second global test timeout because slow Windows CI runners hit it during linking, which caused false failures.
